abstract: Highlights • SIRT5 was down-regulated in the ENKTL, while SIRT5 suppressed the NKTL cell proliferation through desuccinylation effect. • SIRT5 catalyzed the desuccinylation of glycolytic enzyme GPI in ENKTL cells, which accelerated GPI protein degradation through the autophagy-lysosome system. • SIRT5 inhibited glycolysis via mediating the desuccinylation of GPI, and thus suppressing ENKTL cell proliferation.

Methods
Database and bioinformatic analysis
The public dataset
GSE90597
(
https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE90597
) [
19
] was utilized for bioinformatic analysis in this study. The public dataset is composed of 66 cases of NK/T-cell lymphoma tissues, including nodal NK/T-cell lymphoma (NKTL,
n
= 19) and extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma (ENKTL,
n
= 47). ENKTL are further divided into nasal type (20 cases), non-nasopharynx type (15 cases), and unknown type (12 cases). This study selected 20 cases of nasal type ENKTL and 19 cases of NKTL for further contrastive analysis. The differentially expressed genes (DEGs) was screened under the criteria of
p
< 0.05 and log
2
fold change>1.2.
GSE90597
was also used for the next GO enrichment analysis, SIRT5 and GPI expression analysis, OS analysis, and Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA).
ENKTL biopsy specimens
Frozen tumor blocks from 10 patients diagnosed with ENKTL were collected for this study, and 10 normal nasal mucosa (NNM) tissues were served as control. The study was approved by the Ethics Committee of The Third Xiangya Hospital, and was carried out in compliance with the Declaration of Helsinki.
Western blotting and immunoprecipitation
Lysis buffer with protease inhibitor was used to treat the tissues to obtain the protein extracts, which were quantified with a BCA Protein Assay Kit (Abcam, UK). Western blotting was performed according to the standard methods. After isolated with 12 % SDS/PAGE, protein extracts were moved to a PVDF membrane for blocking in 5 % fat-free milk. The antibodies were purchased from manufacturers: Succinyllysine (PTM, PTM-401, dilution at 1:500), anti-CPT1A (Abcam, ab220789, dilution at 1:1000), GPI (Omnimabs,
OM153585
, dilution at 1:400), anti-SIRT5 (Abcam, ab259967, dilution at 1:1000), anti-HA (Ptgcn,51,064–2-AP, dilution at 1:2000), anti-FLAG (Abcam, ab205606, dilution at 1:1000), β-actin (Ptgcn, 66,009–1-Ig, dilution at 1:2000). The membrane was then incubated with HRP-conjugated secondary antibody, followed by development on an enhanced chemiluminescence system (Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA).
For immunoprecipitation assay, total cells were lysed in lysis buffer with protease inhibitor cocktail to obtain the whole lysates. Next, SIRT5 protein immunoprecipitation was achieved by incubation with anti-SIRT5 antibody. The elution was analyzed by western blotting assay. To perform the exogenous Co-IP assay, we constructed FLAG-SIRT5 and HA-GPI (WT) plasmids for transfection into SNK-6 and YTS cells, and IP (HA antibody) and IB were adopted to detect FLAG (SIRT5) and succinylation (Succ). Input was applied to determine HA, FLAG, and β-actin.
Immunohistochemistry (IHC) analysis
Human ENKTL and NNM tissues were embedded in paraffin for cutting into 3 μm slices. Mouse tumor tissues were fixed by 4 % formalin, sealed in paraffin, and sliced into 3 μm thin. After deparaffinization in xylene and hydration in ethyl alcohol, sections were repaired at high pressure for 2 min, followed by incubation in blocking buffer (3 % H
2
O
2
in ddH
2
O) at 25 °C for 10 min. Then the primary antibodies against SIRT5 (abcam, ab259967, dilution at 1:100), GPI (OmnimAbs,
OM153585
, dilution at 1:200), and Ki-67 (proteintech, 27,309–1-AP, dilution at 1:2000) were added and incubated with samples at 4 °C for overnight. After incubation with the secondary antibody at 25 °C for 10 min, sections were developed with a diaminobenzidine chromogen solution for imaging. After re-stained with hematoxylon, dehydrated with gradient alcohol, the sections were mounted in neutral balsam.
Quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) and primers
Total RNA was extracted using the TRIzol reagent. Then cDNA was synthesized using a reverse transcription Kit (FSQ-101 TOYOBO, Japan). SYBR Green PCR Master Mix (Thermo Fisher, USA) used for qRT-PCR reaction on a 7500 Fast Real-time PCR System (Applied Biosystems, USA). Gene expression was normalized to β-actin using the 2
−ΔΔCt
method. The qRT-PCR primers were synthesized by Sangon Biotech (Shanghai, China), and their sequences are as listed below:
SIRT5 F: 5′-TGGCTCGGCCAAGTTCAAGTATG-3′
SIRT5 R: 5′-AAGGTCGGAACACCACTTTCTGC-3′
β-actin F: 5′-TCCATCATGAAGTGTGACG-3′
β-actin R: 5′-TACTCCTGCTTGCTGATCCAC-3′
Cell culture and transfection
SNK-6 cells, an EBV-positive ENKL cell line, were established based on the primary lesion of the ENKTL. Human NKTCL cell line YTS cells were also derived from the primary lesion of the ENKTL. NK-92 and NK-92MI cell lines were purchased from the American Type Culture Collection. Hut-102 cells were purchased from the cell bank of the Shanghai Institute of Biochemistry&Cell biology. The normal NK cells (NNK) were isolated from healthy donors’ blood according to a previous study [
20
]. YTS and Hut-102 cells were cultured in RPMI-1640 medium. SNK6 cells were also in RPMI-1640 medium supplemented with 1000 U/mL recombinant human IL-2 (Sigma-Aldrich). Cell transfection was completed with Lipofectamine 2000 (Invitrogen).
Cell proliferation analysis (CCK8)
Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK8) (Beyotime, C0038) was used for assessing cell proliferation. SNK-6 and YTS cells were seeded in triplicate in 96‐well plates (1 × 10
5
cells per well), and cultured in 100ul medium at suitable condition for 24 h. Afterwards, 10 µl CCK-8 solution was added into and incubated with the cells for 1 h. The absorbance was measured on a Microplate Reader (Molecular Devices, USA). The proliferation rate = OD (treatment group-blank control)/OD (control group-blank control) ×100 %.
Soft-agar colony formation assay
SNK-6 and YTS cells (2 × 10
4
) were plated in 6-well plates containing soft layers at the bottom, and incubated in culture medium with 10 % FBS. Two weeks later, the cells were fixed with 10 % formaldehyde and stained with 0.1 % ctystal violet dye for 1 h. Under a microscope, colonies with >50 cells was counted. Rate of colony formation = (number of colonies/seeded cell number) ×100 %.
Pyruvic acid production detection
Cells were harvested after trypsinization and washed with PBS. The suspension was centrifuged and suspended with PBS. Repeat for three times, and the total cell volume was marked with V1. After lysed with lysis buffer at 4  °C for 10 min, cells were then centrifuged for 10 min, and the total lysis volume was recorded as V2. The pyruvate concentration of the cell lysis supernatant (C1) was detected with a BioVision kit (BioVision technologies, USA). The intracellular pyruvate concentration (C) was computed with the following formula: C = C1×V2/V1.
Quantification of lactate
The standard samples were used to prepare the standard curve. Cells at the same number and volume were seeded in 96-well plate and cultured in RPMI-1640 complete media. After 72 h, culture media were harvested and the cell number at this time was counted for the later normalization. The obtained media was diluted into 1:10 with ddH2O prior to detection with a Lactate Assay Kit (K607–100, Biovision Inc., USA). Concentrations of lactate in samples were examined according to the standard curve as a reference.
Oxygen consumption rate (OCR)
The OCR for ENKTL cells were analyzed according to standard protocols described previously in a study [
21
]. SNK-6 and YTS cells (2 × 104) were incubated in a 96-well plate for overnight. Next, the cells were detected with a Seahorse XF Cell Mitostreses test kit (103,015–100, Agilent, USA), on a Seahorse XFe96 Analyzer (Agilent, USA). Basal OCR was formulated as [OCRinitial−OCRR+
A
].
GPI activity
SNK-6 and YTS cells (1 × 10
4
) were centrifuged at 10,000 g for 15 min to collect the supernatant. Prepare the NADH standard solution: 5 µl NADH solution was diluted with 45 µl GPI Assay buffer (final concentration 1.25 mM). NADH standard solution at different volumes (0, 2, 4, 6,8, 10 µl) were added into the supernatant, with the final concentration to be 0, 2.5, 5, 7.5, 10, and 12.5 nmol. B
=the content of degraded NADH (nmol); Phosphoglucose Isomerase Activity=
B
/(∆OD×
V
) × dilution ratio (mU/ml).
F6P detection
Prepare the standard substance for standard curve: 5 µl F6P standard solution was diluted with 495ul ddH
2
O (final concentration 1 nmol/ul), then add 50 µl F6P solution (1 nmol/ul) into 950ul ddH
2
O (final concentration 50 pmol/ul). The standard solution (50 pmol/ul) (0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 µl) were added into the detecting well. Add F6P Assay Buffer to reach a total volume of 50 µl, and the final concentrations of F6P standard substance were 0,100,200,300,400,600 pmol/well. SNK-6 and YTS cells (1 × 10
4
) were washed and resuspended with PBS, and then centrifuged to collect the supernatant. 50 µl reaction solution was added into each sample well, positive control, and negative control, and the system were culture at 37 °C for 5 min, followed by detecting at Ex/Em=535/587 nm.
4D label-free succinylation modification quantitative proteome
This experiment was performed by Hangzhou Jingjie Biotechnology Co. Ltd. to detect succinylation in SNK-6 cells. SNK-6 cells at different groups were collected and lysed by a lysate buffer under sonication. After enzymatic digestion with trypsin, addition of dithiothreitol and lodoacetamide, cells were treated by IP buffer to eliminate the peptides. Transferred the supernatant to succinylated resin and maintained overnight at 4 °C with a rotary agitator. The eluate was vacuum freeze-dried for analysis by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS).
The resulting LC-MS/MS data were processed using MaxQuant search engine (v.1.6.15.0). Tandem mass spectra were searched against the human SwissProt database (20,422 entries) concatenated with reverse decoy database. Trypsin/P was specified as the cleavage enzyme, with no >2 missing cleavages. The mass tolerance for precursor ions: 20 ppm in first search, and 5 ppm in main search. 0.02 Da was the mass tolerance for fragment ions. The FDR of protein identification was adjusted to 1 %.
Immunofluorescence assay
SNK-6 cells were fixed with 4 % PMSF (Sangon Biotech) and treated with 0.3 % Triton X-100. Afterwards, the cells were blocked with 3 % BSA, followed by adding primary antibodies (anti-SIRT5, 1:250; anti-Flag, 1:500). Lyso-Tracker Green (beyotime), Alex-Fluor-594‐conjugated secondary antibodies, and DAPI (Blue, for cell nucleus staining) were then introduced for color development. A Leica fluorescence optical microscope was used for image capturing. GPI red fluorescence overlaid with lysosome green fluorescence to form a yellow fluorescence. The red fluorescence and yellow fluorescence intensity were measured. The percentage of the colorization was calculated based on the formula: the yellow fluorescence intensity/the red fluorescence intensity × 100 %.
Apoptosis assay
ENKTL cells were treated with 0.25 % trypsin, centrifuged, and resuspended. Then cell apoptosis was evaluated with an Annexin V-FITC/PI Apoptosis Detection Kit (BD Biosciences, USA). With 1 × 10
4
harvested cells resuspended in 500 µl binding buffer, 10 µl Annexin V-FITC reagent was added for staining, followed by 10 µl PI. Cell apoptosis was analyzed by a flow cytometry (BD, USA).
To detect cell apoptosis in tumor tissue of xenograft, we conducted the TUNEL staining in formalin-fixed and paraffin-embedded sections with the One-Step TUNEL Apoptosis Assay Kit (Beyotime Biotechnology, China). The positive apoptotic cells were counted in 5 random fields to calculate the apoptotic rate.
Establishment of xenograft mouse model
10-week-old naked mice were divided into three groups (
n
= 4 in each group). SNK6 cells were grouped by transfecting with Vector NC, SIRT5(KD), or SIRT5(KD)+GPI(KD), and then 100 µl of 1 × 10
5
SNK6 cells were suspended in PBS. Next, 100 µl growth factor-reduced basement membrane matrix (Matrigel™, BD Biosciences) were added into the cell suspension. Then 200 µl of solution was subcutaneously implanted along the mouse flank. From the 7th day, the tumor size was measured each three days using a digital caliper to compute its volume. Twenty-five days later, mice were sacrificed to take the tumor tissues for histopathological examination.
Statistical analysis
All experiments were repeated in triplicated, and data are expressed as mean ± standard deviation (SD). Student's
t
-test was adopted in comparison between two groups, or Mann-Whitney test was performed. For comparison among multiple groups, one-way ANOVA test and Tukey's post hoc test was employed. A p value of <0.05 was defined to be statistically significant. Graphpad prism 8.0 (GraphPad Software, USA) was used for statistical analysis and drawing.
body:
Introduction
Extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type (ENKTL) is a sub-type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma that supposed to be derived from the natural killer, commonly presenting in the nasal cavity [
1
]. Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection is considered as the leading cause of ENKTL development, followed by the ethnic factor [
2
]. ENKTL is prevalent among East Asia and South America, but is rare in western populations [
3
]. Due to the aggressive feature and multi-drug chemoresistance, the prognosis of advanced ENKTL is still dismal [
4
]. What worse, the exact etiology of ENKTL remains ambiguous because of its implicated pathogenesis [
5
]. Therefore, research on the molecular mechanism is urgently needed to improve the therapy strategy and prognosis of ENKTL.
Altered energy metabolism is a remarkable hallmark of cancer cells, to meet their immense demand for energy to achieve proliferation, invasion, and metastasis [
6
]. Aerobic glycolysis is an essential way for energy production by converting glucose into lactate. Recently, targeting glycolysis has been proposed as an attractive method for therapeutic intervention of tumors, and various regulative factors of glycolytic pathway have been paid much attention [
7
]. The deacylase sirtuin 5 (SIRT5) is engaged in regulating cellular homeostasis and activity of proteins implicated in glycolysis, and thus participating in tumor development [
8
]. Nowicki and colleagues have proved the upregulation of SIRT5 during hematopoietic stem cell mobilization in non-Hodgkin lymphoma [
9
]. Our previous analysis based on database showed that SIRT5 mRNA was significantly down-regulated in the ENKTL, and low expression of SIRT5 is accompanied with worse prognosis in ENKTL and NKTL patients. It suggests that SIRT5 may act as an antitumor factor in ENKTL, while its molecular mechanism remains unclear.
Emerging proteomic studies have indicated that lysine succinylation is associated with multiple metabolic processes [
10
]. SIRT5 catalyzes the removal of lysine succinylation modifications from proteins, to participate in various disease pathogenesis [
11
]. For example, SIRT5 contributed to desuccinylation of peroxisomal ACOX1, which helped to relieve peroxisome-induced oxidative stress, and thus restricting hepatocellular carcinoma progression [
12
]. By conducting the succinylation modification quantitative proteomics in ENKTL cells, we observed that SIRT5 mediated the desuccinylation modification of Glucose-6-phosphate isomerase (GPI), a pivotal glycolytic enzyme. Therefore, it can be hypothesized that SIRT5 may modulate glycolysis via mediating desuccinylation of GPI, thereby influencing ENKTL progression.
GPI functions to catalyze the reversible isomerization of d-glucose-6-phosphate (G6P) into d-fructose-6-phosphate (F6P), which is the second catalytic step of glycolysis process [
13
]. Due to the critical role of carbohydrate metabolism in tumor development, GPI has been found to be over-expressed in gastrointestinal and renal [
14
,
15
], breast [
16
], lung [
17
], and endometrial cancers [
18
], and it is correlated with poor prognosis and shorter overall survival (OS). Through bioinformatic analysis, we found GPI was up-regulated in ENKTL than in nodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma (NKTL), and GPI expression was negatively correlated with OS of ENKTL and all natural killer/T-cell lymphoma (NKTCL) patients. It is putative that GPI exerts a significant impact on ENKTL development.
In this study, we are devoted to exploring the action mechanism of SIRT5 regulating ENKTL cell proliferation, in which the role of glycolysis is investigated. In addition, the interaction between SIRT5 and GPI, and its impact on GPI protein expression level, are all the focus that should be placed emphasis on. The current study aims to develop an emerging SIRT5-based antitumor target for ENKTL, as well as glycolysis and glycolysis-related enzymes, to improve the current status of ENKTL therapy

SIRT5 down-regulation in ENKTL is implicated with worse prognosis and tumor glycolysis

SIRT5 is one of the known desuccinylase that mediates the desuccinylation of proteins to influence the occurrence and development of diseases. Through data analysis based on the

SIRT5 functions to catalyze the desuccinylation of GPI in ENKTL cells
We have proven that SIRT5 repressed ENKTL cell proliferation by functioning as a desuccinylase, but its targeted protein remains unclear. Subsequently, we over-expressed SIRT5 in SNK-6 cells and assessed the succinylation modification. Then 201 sites were observed with significantly different in the level of succinylation modification, including 160 sites (corresponding to 53 proteins) in which the succinylation modification level was decreased, and 41 sites (corresponding to 24 proteins) in which the succinylation modification level was increased. That is, the whole succinylation modification level in SNK-6 cells was apparently reduced after SIRT5 over-expression, not only for the modified sites but also the affected proteins.
4D label-free succinylation modification quantitative proteomic further found GPI succinylation modification sites were declined in the SIRT5(OE) group, and succinylation level of K252 and K454 sites were noted to be down-regulated in the SIRT5(OE) group (
Table 1
).

displayed the secondary mass spectrum of protein for GPI succinylation modification identification, including the K252 and K454 sites. GPI is responsible for catalyzing the conversion of G6P into F6P. It implied that SIRT5 may be involved in this step. ), and GPI expression level was negatively correlated with OS, both in ENKTL and in the whole NKTCL patients (

). Hence, high GPI expression may indicate a more favorable prognosis of ENKTL.

Decreased GPI succinylation inhibited ENKTL cell proliferation via preventing glycolysis
Deoxyglucose (2-DG) is a non-metabolizable glucose analog that can block glycolysis and energy generation. In tumor cells, 2-DG inhibits glycolysis and reduced the production of ATP, pyruvic acid, and lactic acid, leading to severe shortage of energy of tumor cells and final apoptosis. Herein, 2-DG was used as the inhibitor of glycolysis to reveal the impact of glycolysis on ENKTL cell proliferation. SIRT5-mediated desuccinylation of GPI protein accelerated its degradation by the autophagy-lysosome system
To figure out the succinylation modification sites of GPI protein, we constructed the plasmids including FLAG-SIRT5, HA-GPI (WT), HA-GPI (K252R), HA-GPI (K454R), and HA-GPI (K252R/K454R). They were transfected into YTS cells and SNK-6 cells before the evaluation of the succinylation level of GPI. In the WT of HA-GPI group, the transfection of FLAG-SIRT5 decreased the succinylation level of GPI compared to the transfection of FLAG-NC. The succinylation levels of HA-GPI (K252R) and HA-GPI (K454R) were lower than that of HA-GPI (WT) in the presence of FLAG-NC. Transfection of FLAG-SIRT5 further decreased the succinylation levels of HA-GPI (K252R) and HA-GPI (K454R). These results suggest that SIRT5 inhibits succinylation at both K252 and K454 sites of GPI. Mutation at both K252 and K454 sites of GPI (K252R/K454R) showed barely undetectable succinylation no matter in the presence of FLAG-NC or FLAG-SIRT5. These results further suggest that there are probably no other site for succinylation in GPI protein apart from K252 and K454 sites (
Fig. 6A
).

Discussion
Herein, the clinical investigation, ENKTL cell experiments, and
in vivo
xenograft mouse experiment collectively proved that the down-regulation of SIRT5 increased the succinylation of GPI protein. As the results, the protein stability of GPI was enhanced, which promoted the glycolysis pathway and ENKTL cell proliferation (
Fig. 8E
). It is the first study highlighting the essential role of SIRT5 in ENKTL cell proliferation by affecting the succinylation of GPI and energy metabolism, suggesting that SIRT5, GPI and succinylation modification could be effective targets for ENKTL therapy.
So far, multiple pathogenic pathways have been ascertained in ENKTL, such as Janus-associated kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription, platelet-derived growth factor, p53/mTOR, NF-кB, and the MELK-EZH2 signaling pathways [
23
]. Nevertheless, a conclusive and uncontroversial molecular mechanism is still needed, to serve as a therapeutic target in the treatment of ENKTL. Herein, we uncovered a SIRT5-GPI regulation axis in the ENKTL pathogenesis. Our data uncovered that SIRT5 was down-regulated in ENKTL tissue and was associated with poor prognosis, and proved that high expression of SIRT5 suppressed ENKTL cell proliferation. SIRT5 is acting as a tumor promoter or suppressor because of its diverse roles in affecting genomic stability, metabolic reprogramming, and tumor microenvironment [
[24]
,
[25]
,
[26]
]. For instance, SIRT5 facilitated lung cancer progression and chemotherapy resistance by up-regulating a transcription factor that involved in oxidative defense [
27
]. SIRT5-mediated SDHA desuccinylation promotes clear cell renal cell carcinoma tumorigenesis [
28
]. However, SIRT5 also functions as a suppressor of lung tumor by inhibiting lung tumor cell proliferation through desuccinylating and activating SOD1 [
29
]. In addition, SIRT5 suppresses tumor growth by regulating mitochondrial metabolism and synaptic remodeling in gliomas [
30
]. It seems that the promoting or suppressive roles of SIRT5 in tumor primarily depends on its downstream targets.
SIRT5 primarily functions as a desuccinylase to remove the lysine acyl modifications in proteins [
31
,
32
]. Our study elucidated that SIRT5 mediated the desuccinylation of GPI, a key enzyme for glycolysis process. SIRT5 has been reported to regulate proteins involved in energy metabolism [
24
]. For instance, SIRT5 desuccinylates pyruvate kinase M2 to reduce its activity [
33
]. The “Warburg effect” has underlined the critical role of aerobic glycolysis for the energy metabolism of tumor cells, rather than mitochondrial OXPHOS [
34
]. Our data indicated that SIRT5 over-expression repressed glycolysis by converting it into OXPHOS, via catalyzing the desuccinylation of GPI. With the succinylation modification reduced in GPI protein, its stability was decreased and was prone to be degraded via the autophagy-lysosome system. It is the first time that the influence of glycolysis on ENKTL progression is exactly certified, and the succinylation modification of GPI and its tumor promoter actor in ENKTL is also originally elucidated. These findings clarify a novel insight into the modulatory mechanism of ENKTL development, providing an innovative perspective for ENKTL basic research and clinical practice.
With the high accessibility of sensitive mass spectrometry method, diverse forms of lysine acylation have been noticed to modify proteins, including lysine acetylation, succinylation, malonylation, and so on [
35
]. Furthermore, protein acylation modifications contribute a lot in regulating gene expression and intracellular signaling, and thereby driving tumorigenesis [
36
]. Until now, histone acetylation modification has been paid attention in ENKTL [
37
], while the other forms of modification have not been identified in this tumor. In the current study, the desuccinylation effect of SIRT5 on GPI protein was newly discovered via the 4D label-free succinylation modification quantitative proteome, which is an emerging technology for succinylation modification quantitative. It is the first time that succinylation modification in GPI protein is detected. Erenow, phosphorylation and ubiquitination are the common models of post-translation modification in GPI protein [
38
,
39
]. 4D label-free succinylation modification quantitative proteome has been applied in disclosing desuccinylation modification of AIFM1 by SIRT5, in which SIRT5 protects the intervertebral disc from degeneration [
40
]. With the advance of this technology, more types of lysine acylation are expected in the future, as well their impact on tumor tumorigenesis.
In conclusion, SIRT5 plays important role in glycolysis pathway, ENKTL cell proliferation and the tumor growth, by altering the succinylation of GPI protein and its protein stability. This study provides solid theoretical basis for improving therapy efficacy and prognosis in ENKTL.
